I am not sure about not having FermionicMapper etc as part of docs. If say I look at ParityMapper in the current resultant docs I can see some method, that pretty much as a end user of the mapper I should not care about. But I don't, unlike before, see any `map` method, the one and only thing as an end user I normally would use. I cannot navigate up the class structure to see what it may inherit since the FermionicMapper link there is not operational, although maybe that class won't show map there either. If I happen to know its QubitMapper (now I would be able to go up once again from FermionicMapper were that included) I can go there, though then I see it more as a generic map method taking a SparseLabelOp. Maybe that common base method is all we would get now anyway. For any classes etc that are exposed to an end user, or developer to extend, we have normally included them. Maybe its not a lot better in regards of how map method gets exposed with including it  (not sure)  but at least one can navigate up through the parents in the docs.

Thanks for raising this! I think this is actually a symptom of the underlying issue that we do not document inherited members in our classes. I have fixed this for the `mappers` module in the last commit but I think we should revisit this choice for all docs in a separate PR.
In fact, Qiskit Terra also already differentiates between two cases where classes should document the inherited members and where they should not. For the ad-hoc fix here, I mirrored that (actually the inverse because our default is the opposite). We should revisit this in a separate step and align our docs with that of Terra. I will open a separate issue for this shortly.
